input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on us. Every exclusivity reference runs the other way or is neutral: the licence is expressly "Non Exclusive" (Preamble, p0030, p0049, p0052), and Licensor retains the right to license the technology to others (p0043) — i.e. no exclusivity is granted to us and none is demanded of us. There is no requirements commitment, no covenant not to procure FX technology or services from third parties, and no obligation to route volume solely through the Platform (searches for "sole"/"exclusive"/"third party"/"all transactions" return nothing of that kind). The defined term flagged in the planner hint, "Right of First Refusal" (Article XXII, p0139), is a change-of-control/exit right — a 5-business-day right to match a third-party offer to buy Licensee's assets or merge with Licensee — not a restriction on sourcing alternative suppliers, and it expressly releases us to close with the third party if not exercised (p0140–p0141). The restrictions in Article II (e.g. p0027, p0041, p0044) are ordinary licence-scope and anti-sublicensing limits on use of Licensor's own technology, not exclusive-dealing covenants. This meets the preferred position (no exclusivity binding Customer); no redline required. Noted for the record only: the ROFR and the Change of Control provision (p0134) constrain our exit flexibility and are separately reviewable under assignment/change-of-control rules, not under this rule.
